LESSON GOALS
•	 To understand simple stories and conversations.
•	 To give and follow simple directions and instructions.
•	 To ask and answer questions about familiar topics 
(personal information, clothes, colours, weather, etc.).
•	 To understand and talk about dates and numbers.
•	 To talk about things you can see in different places 
in the world and things you can buy or do in a shop.
MATERIALS
•	 TR#4 What Do You Do?
•	 TR#12 The Toyshop Song

at least half of the recommended activities up to this point.

3.– WORKSHEET: FIND THE ODD ONE OUT (PP.5-6) (9’)
Find the Odd One Out

NOTE: if you collected your Ss books during the booklet 
activity, have them ask you for it now by saying “Can I have 
my book please?”; otherwise, ask them to take it out of their 
bag. Explain the activity before giving out the books/asking Ss 
to take them out since they might get distracted.
MATERIALS
•	 10 red stickers per S or one red crayon per S
This worksheet shows 10 shops along with items which can 
or can’t be bought there.
Have the Ss ask for the materials (stickers or crayons) by 
saying, “Can I have…, please?”
To complete the worksheet, ask each S what can be bought 
at each of the shops by saying, “What can you buy at the...?”. 
The S must look at the items below the shop and identify what 
can or can’t be bought there using the structure, “At the … you 
can buy… but you can’t buy...”. Then all the Ss put a red sticker 
on the items that cannot be bought there.
We want to stress the use of “but” in this structure, so we 
suggest you add a gesture like raising your finger whenever you 
say it. This will help Ss notice the word and identify its meaning. 
To follow up, ask each S where one of the items in red can 
be bought. For example, if there is some pasta below the ice 
cream parlour, ask a S, “You can buy pasta at the ice cream 
parlour, is that right or wrong?” and have them respond, “No, 
that’s wrong. You can’t buy pasta at the ice cream parlour. You 
can buy ice cream at the ice cream parlour.”

KEY
Fishmonger’s: “At the fishmonger’s you can buy fish BUT 
you can’t buy bread or lollies.”
Bookshop: “At the bookshop can buy books BUT you can’t 
buy newspapers or bananas.”
NOTE: if your Ss think that newspapers can be bought at 
the bookshop, you can accept their answer. Just note you will 
need one more sticker.
Butcher’s: “At the butcher’s you can buy sausages BUT 
you can’t buy pasta or sweets.”
Greengrocer’s: “At the greengrocer’s you can buy lettuce 
BUT you can’t buy sandals or chips.”
Toyshop: “At the toyshop you can buy videogames BUT 
you can’t buy hot chocolate or fizzy drinks.”
Ice cream parlour: “At the ice cream parlour you can buy 
ice cream BUT you can’t buy pasta or jumpers.”
Bakery: “At the bakery can buy muffins BUT you can’t 
buy lettuce or sausages.”
Pet Shop: “At the pet shop you can buy cat food BUT you 
can’t buy chocolate or fish.”
Clothes shop: “At the clothes shop you can buy jumpers 
BUT you can’t buy roller skates or cereal.”
Café: “At the café you can buy fizzy drinks BUT you can’t 
buy chocolate or footballs.”
NOTE: if your Ss think that chocolate can be bought at the 
café, you can accept their answer. Just note you will need one 
more sticker.

> Scenario A
If your group has achieved the activity goal on My Way (i.e., 
they have done all or most of the activities in the current Mission), 
say, “You’re doing amazing on My Way! You have played lots 
of games in Mission 2, so we can do a special sticker activity 
together!”. Take the Day 3 stickers and have them ask, “Can I 
have some stickers, please?”. Do the activity as instructed below. 
> Scenario B
If your group hasn’t reached the activity goal on My Way, 
simply move on with the class. You will have to complete one 
or two activities from the bonus section to make up for the 
time allotted to this dynamic. 
The point of this activity is to review the shops in a fun 
way using the sticker pages. Ss have to stick the stickers and 
answer the questions by following the white lines. Model the 
task by looking for the stickers, sticking them, and answering 
the questions. 
Have Ss open pp.14-15 (sticker pages section) and say, “Let’s 
find out where the characters are going!”. Point to circle number 
one and ask, “What number is this?”. Ss should respond, “It’s 
number 1!”. Say, “Can you find number 1 on the sticker sheet?”, 
and elicit, “Here it is!”. Do the same for sticker 2. 
Then, move on to the rectangles. Point to number three and 
ask, “What number is this?”. Ss should respond, “It’s number 
3!”. Say, “Can you find number 3 on the sticker sheet? What 
is it?”, and elicit, “Here it is! It’s the bakery!”. Now ask, “Who 
is going to the bakery?”. Let Ss trace the path with their finger 
and answer, “Dad is going to the bakery!”. Follow the same 
procedure for stickers 4-8 and do as many as time allows.
We recommend making this activity more dynamic by making 
it a competition to answer the questions as fast as possible. 
You can give points to Ss who respond correctly.

If you can’t finish the whole activity, tell the Ss that they can 
continue at home.
KEY (From top to bottom, left to right)
Sticker 3: Who is going to the bakery? Dad is going to 
the bakery.
Sticker 4: Who is going to the fishmonger’s? Mum is 
going to the fishmonger’s.
Sticker 5: Who is going to the greengrocer’s? Grandpa 
is going to the greengrocer’s.
Sticker 6: Who is going to the toyshop? Pam is going to 
the toyshop.
Sticker 7: Who is going to the butcher’s? Grandma is 
going to the butcher’s.
Sticker 8: Who is going to the newsagent’s? Paul is going 
to the newsagent’s.

> How to Play
Each S will take a food cutout from a cloth bag and their 
classmates will help them to stick it on the Supermarket sheet 
(P.2.2) by giving them instructions on where to place it.

> Warm-Up
Quickly review the prepositions using your hands: next to, 
between, behind, in front of and opposite. Then review the names 
of the different cutouts found in the cloth bag by asking, “What 
are these?/What is this?” and get the S to reply using a full 
structure, “They are cherries./It is a turkey!”. Continue in this 
manner until you have gone over all the food items. 
> Main Activity
Put all the activity cutouts in a cloth bag. Pair up the Ss (S1 and 
S2). Tell the Ss, “Let’s put the food items in the supermarket!”. 
To do the activity, proceed as follows:
•	 S1: Takes a food cutout. 
•	 S2: “What have you got?” 
•	 S1: “I’ve got lettuce.” 
•	 S2: “Where does the lettuce go?”
•	 S1: “The lettuce goes ....” and places the cutout on the 
correct spot using Blu-Tack.
> Follow-Up
To follow up, ask Ss where the different items are. For example, 
“Jane, where does the lettuce go?”, to which Jane will have to 
answer, “The lettuce goes next to the cherries.”
7.– ACTIVITY 3: CAN YOU TELL ME THE WAY?  
(VERSION 1) (8’)
P.2.3
P.2.3
TARGET LANGUAGE

Go past
Go straight ahead
Turn left
Behind
On your right
On your left
Opposite
Next to
Between

> How to Play
In this game, the Ss must tell their classmate the way to get 
to the correct shop to buy a certain item.
> Warm-Up
Quickly review the name of the items (P.2.3) with the Ss and 
where they can buy them. Ask “Where can you buy a dress?” to 
which they should answer, “You can buy a dress at the clothes 
shop.” If needed, review the shops on the A3 that your Ss find 
tricky (such as charity shop, town hall, dentist, basketball court, 
football pitch, etc.)
> Main Activity
Pair the Ss up (S1 and S2). Put the Item memory cards (P.2.3) 
face down on the table. To do the activity, proceed as detailed 
below. We highly encourage you to model the steps with a S 
first. Say, “Let’s go explore the city!”. Then proceed as follows:
•	 S1: Takes a bike cutout and turns over an item card.
•	 T: “What do you need to buy?”
•	 S1: “I need to buy dog food.” (or whatever item is on 
the card). 
•	 T: “Where can you buy dog food?”
•	 S2: “You can buy dog food at the pet shop.”
•	 T: “S1, you are at the bookshop.”
•	 S1: “Can you tell me the way (to the pet shop), please?”
•	 S2: Gives directions accordingly. For example: “To get 
to the pet shop, turn right. Go straight ahead and go 
past the supermarket and the sports centre. At the 
sports centre turn left. You will find the pet shop on 
your right/the pet shop is opposite the charity shop.”
> Follow-Up
Ask Ss about the location of different shops. For example: 
“John, where is the greengrocer’s?” to which they should reply, 
“The greengrocer’s is between the bakery and the charity 
shop.”
8.– ACTIVITY 8: TAKE A WALK (VERSION 2) (TR#15) (5’)
P.2.5

> How to Play
This version of this activity is played like the musical chairs 
game.
Stick up the Shop cards (P.2.5) that appear in Take a Walk 
Version 2 (TR#15) (pet shop, ice cream parlour, clothes shop, 
toyshop and bakery) around the room. Look at the lyrics and 
try not to place the shops that are sung one after another too 
close together. 
> Warm-Up
If you feel it is necessary, quickly drill the names of the 
different shops or places.
To do this without taking the cards off the wall, walk around 
the room and ask Ss to shout out the different names saying, 
“It’s the clothes shop! It’s the bakery!”, etc.
> Main Activity
Introduce the activity by saying, “Let’s take a walk around 
town!”. Next, play the song Take A Walk Version 2 (TR#15). 
Ss must sing along to the song and walk around the room and 
when they hear one of the shops or places being mentioned, 
they must go and point to that place.
During the musical interlude, encourage Ss to ask, “Where 
shall we go next?”
> Follow-Up
If time allows, ask each S, “What can you buy at the...?” 
and the Ss individually, each saying a different item, should 
say, “You can buy ... at the...”. Challenge them to come up with 
items they haven’t learned in class.

10.– TIME TO GO HOME (TR#20) (2’) 
Sing the Time to Go Home song and have the Ss form a line

BONUS
ACTIVITY 6: FREEZE!
P.2.5
> Main Activity
The Ss sit on the floor in a circle. Tell them, “Let’s see if 
you remember what you can buy at each shop!”. Place the 
pile of Shop cards (P.2.5) face down in the middle of the circle 
and get the Ss to begin passing the ball. Tell them that when 
you say “Freeze!”, they must stop. Whenever you feel like it, 
shout out “FREEZE!” and the S holding the ball must pick up 
a card from the middle of the circle and answer the question, 
“What can you buy at the…?” as quickly as possible. Once Ss 
are used to the game you can make it more dynamic by not 
asking them the question and letting them come up with the 
sentence themselves. For example:
•	 You can buy jumpers at the clothes shop.
•	 You can buy video games at the toy shop.
•	 You can buy muffins at the bakery.
NOTE: you can also play songs from the story to make it 
more dynamic. You can still say “Freeze!” every time you pause 
the song.
> Follow-Up
To follow-up, try to confuse your Ss by saying wrong statements 
about the different shops, for example, “You can buy tomatoes 
at the shoe shop.” to which Ss should answer, “No, you can’t. 
You can buy tomatoes at the greengrocer’s.”

ACTIVITY 7: DIRECTIONS SONG (TR#13) 
> Main Activity
To perform the song, have the Ss stand with their back against 
the wall in a line, side by side. Then the first time they sing the 
song they will simply turn left and right while standing in place 
and then walk straight ahead when the song says to do so. 
The second time you do the activity, they must line up behind 
one another forming a train, holding onto the shoulders of the 
S in front of them. Then, this time, when the song says turn left 
and right, they will actually walk around the room while doing 
so. The song will speed up so make sure the Ss are ready to 
do the actions quickly.
